The minimum vertex cover must contain at least one vertex of every edge of the graph. Thus, it must contain at least one vertex from every set of vertices that form an edge. Thus, it must contain at least n vertices. Conversely, suppose we have a vertex cover with k vertices. For any edge of the graph, it must be incident to one of the k vertices, so it is contained in the vertex cover. Thus, k is a lower bound on the size of the minimum vertex cover. Therefore, we can solve the minimum vertex cover problem in polynomial time by simply using a greedy algorithm. The answer is (E).
